results.corrected_claim: The current (Xcode 27) Apple docs give `func tint(_ color: Color?) -> Glass` and `func interactive(_ isEnabled: Bool = true) -> Glass`. `struct Glass` has exactly five members: `static var regular`, `static var clear`, `static var identity`, `tint(_:)` and `interactive(_:)`. It conforms to Equatable, Sendable and SendableMetatype. Availability is iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS and watchOS 26.0+, with no visionOS entry. The June 2026 and September 2026 SwiftUI update sections add nothing to Glass. The skill's `tint(_ color: Color)` is too narrow because it hides that nil is accepted. The skill's internal name `isInteractive` is wrong (Apple uses `isEnabled`), but that is cosmetic because the external label is `_`.
results.notes: Sources: the DocC JSON for glass, glass/tint(_:) and glass/interactive(_:), all quoted verbatim. Glass's topics list only Instance Methods (interactive(_:), tint(_:)) and Type Properties (clear, identity, regular). The tint(_:) page has no discussion; its abstract is 'Returns a copy of the structure with a configured tint color.' So 'nil clears the tint' follows from the `Color?` type but is not stated in the docs. Existing skill code that passes non-nil colors still compiles. The skill error only matters as documentation.

results.corrected_claim: The type is `@MainActor @preconcurrency struct GlassEffectContainer<Content> where Content : View`. It conforms to View, Sendable and SendableMetatype, on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS and watchOS 26.0+ (no visionOS entry). It has only one initializer: `@MainActor @preconcurrency init(spacing: CGFloat? = nil, @ContentBuilder content: () -> Content)`. `GlassEffectContainer { ... }` works through the nil default; there is no separate `init(content:)`. `ContentBuilder` is declared as `typealias ContentBuilder = ViewBuilder` and arrives with Xcode 27. Apple's SwiftUI updates page (June 2026) says 'Build your project in Xcode 27 or later to construct type-agnostic content from closures that you mark with ContentBuilder…'. So writing `@ViewBuilder` in the skill's signature is equivalent.
results.notes: In the init's declaration tokens, the attribute links to doc://.../SwiftUI/ContentBuilder (precise ID s:7SwiftUI14ContentBuildera). The ContentBuilder page lists platforms iOS 13.0+ and macOS 10.15+, and calls it 'the unified replacement for type-specific builders like ToolbarContentBuilder and CommandsBuilder'. WWDC26 session 269 (What's new in SwiftUI) says: 'ContentBuilder can be used with any minimum deployment target, because under the hood, it's an evolution of the existing ViewBuilder.' The skill's two-init block is inaccurate in form but harmless at call sites.

results.corrected_claim: The overload for a bottom bar is `nonisolated func safeAreaBar(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, @ContentBuilder content: () -> some View) -> some View`, available on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS 26.0+. Its return value reads: 'A new view that displays content above or below the modified view, making space for the content view by vertically insetting the modified view, adjusting the safe area and scroll edge effects to match.' Its discussion reads: 'Similar to the safeAreaInset(edge:alignment:spacing:content:) modifier… Additionally, it extends the edge effect of any scroll views affected by the inset safe area.' Apple's 'Adopting Liquid Glass' article recommends it: 'If you use a custom bar with elements like controls, text, or icons that have content scrolling beneath them, you can register those views to use a scroll edge effect with these APIs: safeAreaBar(edge:alignment:spacing:content:)'. safeAreaInset is not wrong, but it does not register the scroll edge effect.
results.notes: There is a small problem with the quote. The finding's quote ('displays content beside the modified view…') is verbatim Apple text, but it comes from the sibling HorizontalEdge overload. That overload is also what the unsuffixed evidence URL resolves to. The VerticalEdge declaration the finding gives lives at the -9hwgb path. The skill lines are verified: glass-floating-toolbar.md:61, 06-ChatScreen.swift:40 and 05-DashboardScreen.swift:69. I found no 'Fixed' entry for it in the iOS 26.2, 26.3, 26.4 or 27.0 release notes I read. Test focus behavior, or keep safeAreaInset for text-input bars.

results.corrected_claim: The declaration is `nonisolated static func glass(_ glass: Glass) -> Self`, 'Available when Self is GlassButtonStyle.' Its abstract reads 'A button style that applies a configurable Liquid Glass effect based on the button's context.' Its discussion reads 'This button style applies a Liquid Glass effect that you can customize by specifying a tint or variant', with the example `.buttonStyle(.glass(.clear))`. The docs give conflicting availability. The glass(_:) page says 26.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS and watchOS. `GlassButtonStyle.init(_ glass: Glass)` (declared `nonisolated init(_ glass: Glass)`) says 26.1 on the same platforms, while `GlassButtonStyle.init()` says 26.0. Apple's 'Adopting Liquid Glass' lists PrimitiveButtonStyle.glass, glassProminent and glass(_:) as the button styles to use. Every `.glass(x)` produces a GlassButtonStyle, so `.buttonStyle(.glass(isSelected ? .regular.tint(.accentColor) : .regular))` type-checks without branching. It renders tinted regular glass, which is not the same look as `.glassProminent`. There is no `glassProminent(_:)`.

results.corrected_claim: Glass has no `opacity` member. Its only members are regular, clear, identity, tint(_:) and interactive(_:), and it conforms only to Equatable, Sendable and SendableMetatype, not to View or ShapeStyle. So `.glassEffect(.regular.tint(.purple).opacity(0.9))` fails to compile: the implicit member chain ends in Glass, which has no opacity. The compilable equivalent is `.glassEffect(.regular.tint(.purple.opacity(0.9)))`. It uses `Color.opacity(_ opacity: Double) -> Color` (iOS 13.0+, macOS 10.15+) inside the `Color?` argument of `tint(_:)`.
results.notes: The skill line is verified at references/07-anti-patterns.md:93.
